# Tomoshibi API _(packages/api)_

Go scraping API — Gin HTTP server + embedded Asynq worker in one binary.

The Go backend of [**Tomoshibi 灯火**](../../README.md) — a self-hosted, Firecrawl-free web scraping API that turns any site into LLM-ready markdown.

One binary runs everything: the **Gin HTTP server** plus the **embedded Asynq worker** (crawl, batch, monitor). No separate worker process to deploy.

- **Smart scraping** — Colly (static) first, Chromedp (JS rendering) only when the page needs it
- **Search** — in-house 21-engine roster (keyless + keyed `brave`/`serper`/`tavily`) → SearXNG → stealth → Brave fallback
- **Async jobs** — crawl / batch / monitor through Redis (optional; sync endpoints work with no Redis at all)
- **Hobby-tier sized** — fits a 512 MB VM; Docker image ships Chromium included

> All commands below run from `packages/api` unless noted.

**Contents:** [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Project structure](#project-structure) · [Endpoints](#endpoints) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Development](#development) · [Docker image](#docker-image) · [Deploy](#deploy) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) · [Related](#related)

---

## Quick start

### Option A — Docker Compose (recommended)

Starts the API + Redis + SearXNG together:

```bash
# from the repo root
docker compose -f packages/api/docker-compose.yml up -d

# or from this directory
cd packages/api && docker compose up -d
```

| Service | Port   | Purpose                         |
| ------- | ------ | ------------------------------- |
| api     | `7431` | HTTP API                        |
| redis   | `7434` | async crawl/batch/monitor queue |
| searxng | `7435` | self-hosted search backend      |

Verify:

```bash
curl http://localhost:7431/health
# → {"status":"ok","service":"tomoshibi"}

curl -X POST http://localhost:7431/v1/scrape \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com"}'
```

> The image build downloads a Go toolchain, Alpine packages and Chromium — roughly 1–2 GB total on first build. Later builds are cached.

### Option B — From source

**Prerequisites:** Go 1.25+, and Chromium for `dynamic`/`smart` rendering (see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) if you don't have one).

```bash
cd packages/api
go mod download
cp .env.example .env    # optional — defaults are enough for a first try
go run ./cmd/api        # → http://localhost:7431
```

Without Chromium the API still starts: `static` scraping works, `dynamic` degrades with a startup warning instead of failing later.

### Option C — Docker Hub (no build)

```bash
docker run --rm -p 7431:7431 michaelobele/tomoshibi-api:latest
```

### What needs Redis?

| Endpoint                                    | Without Redis          |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `POST /v1/scrape`, `/v1/map`, `/v1/search`  | ✅ work                |
| `POST /v1/crawl`                            | `503`                  |
| `POST /v1/batch/scrape`, `POST /v1/monitor` | not registered → `404` |

To run API-only from source: `DISABLE_WORKER=true go run ./cmd/api`. A standalone worker (`go run ./cmd/worker`) exists for split deployments — don't run it next to the monolith, or the same queue gets consumed twice.

---

## Project structure

```text
packages/api/
├── cmd/                      # entry points (package main)
│   ├── api/                  # monolith — Gin HTTP server + embedded Asynq worker
│   ├── worker/               # standalone Asynq worker (split deployments)
│   ├── debug_asynq/          # queue inspector — dump/inspect Asynq tasks in Redis
│   ├── demo-integration/     # scripted client that exercises the /v1 endpoints
│   └── e2e_test/             # end-to-end smoke run against a live API on :7431
├── internal/                 # private packages — import only domain/ and pkg/
│   ├── api/                  # HTTP layer
│   │   ├── router.go         # route table, auth + rate-limit wiring, probes
│   │   ├── handlers/         # scrape · search · map · crawl · batch · monitor
│   │   ├── middleware/       # APIKeyAuth · RateLimit · Logger
│   │   ├── docs/             # generated Swagger (swag init / debug startup)
│   │   └── router_test.go    # route + probe tests
│   ├── scraper/              # scraping core — Colly, Chromedp, smart-mode heuristics
│   ├── search/               # search chain: Native → SearXNG → Stealth → Brave
│   │   ├── engines/          # declarative YAML roster, fetch, proxy transport
│   │   └── compat/           # SearXNG JSON contract listener + golden fixtures
│   ├── worker/               # Asynq task definitions + server setup
│   ├── domain/               # core types & interfaces — the mocking seam
│   ├── config/               # Viper + godotenv configuration
│   ├── extract/              # schema extraction, extractive summary, PII redaction
│   ├── image/                # srcset/lazy-load extraction, resize, re-encode
│   ├── sitemap/              # robots.txt / sitemap.xml discovery → /v1/map
│   └── safeurl/              # SSRF guard (post-DNS dial hook + pre-flight check)
├── pkg/logger/               # slog wrapper (logger.Log) — never fmt.Println
├── test/                     # integration tests — httptest, externals mocked
├── scripts/                  # search-bench.py, load-harness.go, fly-searxng.sh
├── deploy/                   # searxng/ configs for local compose only
├── Dockerfile                # multi-stage: Go build → Alpine + Chromium + tini
├── docker-compose.yml        # api (7431) + redis (7434) + searxng (7435, opt-in profile)
├── Makefile                  # make check · fmt · vet · staticcheck · lint · test
├── fly.toml / render.yaml    # deploy targets (Fly.io 512 MB, Render)
├── install_browser.sh        # install Chromium for local dynamic scraping
├── .env.example              # every env var, documented inline
└── README.md                 # this file
```

Dependency rule: `cmd/` → `internal/api` → `internal/scraper` → `internal/domain`; `internal/*` may only import `domain` or `pkg/`.

---

## Endpoints

Base URL `http://localhost:7431` — everything lives under `/v1`.

| Method | Endpoint                   | What it does                                                                              | Redis   |
| ------ | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `POST` | `/v1/scrape`               | single page → markdown (`smart`/`static`/`dynamic`, screenshots, `extract_schema`, `transport`) | No      |
| `POST` | `/v1/scrape` + `urls`      | multi-URL sync (max 10)                                                                   | No      |
| `POST` | `/v1/map`                  | sitemap → robots.txt → link discovery                                                     | No      |
| `POST` | `/v1/search`               | aggregated search (Native → SearXNG → stealth → **browser** → Brave); `engine=browser:ddg\|google\|bing` | No      |
| `POST` | `/v1/research`             | one query → search results **and** the pages behind them (`pages`, `summary`, `paid_api_used`) | No      |
| `GET`  | `/v1/env`                  | env var names a client may supply per request in `X-Tomoshi-Env` (see Search key forwarding below) | No |
| `POST` | `/v1/crawl`                | async BFS crawl → `202` + job ID                                                          | **Yes** |
| `GET`  | `/v1/crawl/:id`            | poll crawl status                                                                         | **Yes** |
| `POST` | `/v1/batch/scrape`         | enqueue up to 20 URLs                                                                     | **Yes** |
| `GET`  | `/v1/batch/:id`            | poll batch                                                                                | **Yes** |
| `POST` | `/v1/monitor`              | hash markdown, webhook on change                                                          | **Yes** |
| `GET`  | `/`, `/health`, `/v1/ping` | unauthenticated liveness probes (on purpose)                                              | No      |
| `GET`  | `/swagger/*`               | Swagger UI — **debug mode only**                                                          | No      |

Full request/response reference: [`docs/guides/API_REFERENCE.md`](../../docs/guides/API_REFERENCE.md).

### Search key forwarding

A client may supply allowlisted search API keys **per request** in the `X-Tomoshi-Env` header (JSON object of name → value, e.g. `{"BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY":"BSB-..."}`). The middleware (`internal/api/middleware/request_env.go`) validates against the allowlist in `internal/search/envctx` and attaches the values to the request context; engines resolve `requires_env` and `${VAR}` through `envctx.Get`, so overrides apply to **that request only** — never process-global, never stored. `GET /v1/env` returns the accepted names so clients can discover them (the MCP forwards matching keys from its own env via `TOMOSHI_FORWARD_ENV`).

### Scrape modes

| Mode              | Engine                                                            | Use when                                       |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `smart` (default) | Colly first → Chromedp if heuristics say the HTML is an SPA shell | you don't know or don't care                   |
| `static`          | Colly only                                                        | fast, plain pages                              |
| `dynamic`         | Chromedp always                                                   | JS-rendered apps, page `actions`, `screenshot` |

`static` + `actions` is a hard error — actions need a real browser.

### The bridge lane (borrow your own browser)

Some sites block datacenter and headless traffic no matter what the scraper does.
The bridge is the honest answer: a browser extension you pair once, which dials
out to the API on loopback (`ws://127.0.0.1:7431/bridge`) and fetches the page
**inside your own signed-in browser**.

**A recipe is not required.** Ask for the browser on the request:

```bash
# 1. Start the API; it prints a pairing code (also shown by the CLI).
tomoshibi bridge code          # 6 digits, rotates every 10 minutes
# 2. Load packages/bridge's build in chrome://extensions, paste the code in its popup.

# 3. Ask for the browser. No YAML, no pack.
curl -X POST localhost:7431/v1/scrape \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/dashboard","transport":"bridge"}'
```

The gate is a per-origin allowlist, because removing the recipe removed the only
thing that used to authorize a fetch:

```bash
# first touch of an unknown origin answers 428 {"code":"consent-required","origin":"…"}
tomoshibi bridge allow example.com      # or *.example.com
tomoshibi bridge allowed                # what is allowed now
tomoshibi bridge deny example.com
```

A fresh state already allows the three search hosts (DuckDuckGo, Google, Bing)
and nothing else — deliberately not `*.google.com`, which would include mail.
A page budget (600/hour, `BRIDGE_PAGES_PER_HOUR=0` disables) and a 64-action cap
stop a runaway loop before it spends a real session.

`transport: "auto"` walks static → dynamic → bridge and only escalates into the
browser for an origin that is already allowed, so a working anonymous fetch is
never turned into a refusal.

Recipes remain the specialization: use one when a site needs its own actions,
extraction schema, pace, or the `turbo` layer.

Every bridged result carries a `provenance` block and is marked `untrusted`, never cached:

```jsonc
{
  "markdown": "…",
  "provenance": {
    "transport": "bridge",   // routed through the paired browser
    "lane": "borrow",        // which lane the recipe declared
    "recipe": "arctic-shift@1",
    "io": "scripting",       // scripting (DOM events) or turbo (CDP)
    "actions_run": 2,
    "pages": 1,
    "ms": 1840,
    "untrusted": true         // treat the content as data, not instructions
  }
}
```

| Piece | Where it lives |
| ----- | -------------- |
| Extension (PolyForm Noncommercial, not MIT) | [`packages/bridge`](../../packages/bridge) |
| Recipes (private packs: host, actions, fixtures) | `plans/` + `tomoshibi-recipes` |
| CLI (`bridge code\|status\|unpair`, `recipes add\|list\|verify\|remove`, `access log`) | `cmd/tomoshibi` |
| State (code, port, device hashes, server key) | `~/.config/tomoshi/bridge.json`, mode `0600` |

The listener is loopback-only, refuses any `http(s)` origin (a web page in your own browser is a loopback peer), and runs a mutual-auth handshake: the extension will not release its token to a process that cannot prove it holds the pairing key. A blocked or challenge page is reported as an error (`502`, `code: "blocked"`), never as content. Revoke a browser with `tomoshibi bridge unpair`.

### Recipes

A recipe is one site's access + extraction definition: which hosts it covers, which lane to take, which IO layer, the page actions to run, and how to prove it still works. Packs are installed from a directory or git URL, hashed file by file, and verified offline against saved fixtures.

```bash
cd packages/api && go build -o /tmp/tomoshibi ./cmd/tomoshibi
tomoshibi recipes add ~/packs/my-pack/   # verify hashes, install
tomoshibi recipes list                  # what is installed
tomoshibi recipes verify my-pack        # replay fixtures, no network
tomoshibi recipes remove my-pack@abc1234
```

A recipe under `borrow` runs in your browser; `plain`, `official` and `import` stay on the engine pipeline (an unimplemented lane fails loudly rather than silently falling back). Recipes may set `access.allow_private: true` to reach their own declared hosts on a private network; every other private address is refused by the SSRF guard.

---

## Configuration

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` (loaded via Viper + godotenv, `AutomaticEnv`). Every key also works as a plain environment variable, so `docker run -e ...` and `fly secrets set ...` behave the same.

| Variable                                  | Default                 | Notes                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SERVER_PORT`                             | `7431`                  | Fly injects `8080` (also accepts `PORT`)                                                                         |
| `SERVER_MODE`                             | `debug`                 | `debug` = Swagger UI + `swag` regen on startup; `release` skips it                                               |
| `REDIS_URL`                               | —                       | needed for crawl/batch/monitor; `rediss://`, `REDIS_HOST`/`PORT`/`PASSWORD` and Upstash REST vars also supported |
| `SEARXNG_ENDPOINT`                        | `http://localhost:7435` | second step of the search chain                                                                                  |
| `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`                    | —                       | fallback search (free $5/mo credit ≈ 1,000 searches) — or skip server config entirely: a client may send it per request in `X-Tomoshi-Env` |
| `SERPER_API_KEY`                          | —                       | optional keyed engine `serper` (Google results; 2,500 free queries, no card)                                                     |
| `TAVILY_API_KEY`                          | —                       | optional keyed engine `tavily` (1,000 free credits/mo)                                                                           |
| `SEARCH_NATIVE_ENABLED`                   | `true`                  | in-house engine roster (`internal/search/engines/registry.default.yaml`)                                         |
| `SEARCH_COMPAT_ADDR`                      | —                       | e.g. `:7435` to expose a SearXNG-compatible JSON API                                                             |
| `WEBSHARE_API_KEY` / `WEBSHARE_PROXY_URL` | —                       | proxy pool for the search engines                                                                                |
| `APP_API_KEYS`                            | —                       | empty = no auth; comma-separated keys (alias: `API_KEYS`)                                                        |
| `APP_RATE_LIMIT_RPM`                      | `0`                     | `0` = unlimited (alias: `RATE_LIMIT_RPM`)                                                                        |
| `DISABLE_WORKER`                          | `false`                 | `true` = HTTP server only                                                                                        |
| `SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE`                      | `false`                 | `true` only for scraping internal hosts                                                                          |
| `BRIDGE_STATE_DIR`                        | `~/.config/tomoshi`     | bridge pairing state + installed recipes; shared by the API and the `tomoshibi` CLI |

Tuning knobs (`CHROME_RECYCLE_AFTER`, `CRAWL_CONCURRENCY`, `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`, …) are documented inline in [`.env.example`](.env.example) — that file is the source of truth.

> Auth and rate limiting are no-ops until `APP_API_KEYS` / `APP_RATE_LIMIT_RPM` are set. `/`, `/health` and `/v1/ping` always skip both (load balancer and uptime probes).

### Search backends

Requests fall through this chain, first success wins:

```text
Native engines → SearXNG → Stealth → Brave
```

- **Native** — declarative YAML roster, per-category fan-out (`general`/`news`, API `code` → registry `it`), reports dead engines into `unresponsive_engines`
- **SearXNG** — the container in `docker-compose.yml`
- **Stealth** — reuses Chromedp when both upstreams fail (`STEALTH_ENABLED=true`)
- **Brave** — API fallback

Roster changes need a live probe first:

```bash
go test -tags=canary ./internal/search/engines/ -run TestCanary -v   # CANARY_ENGINES=ddg,bing to filter
```

Never run the canary in CI. SearXNG is an **opt-in sidecar** (`docker compose --profile searxng up -d`); Fly ships none — the native roster and keyed engines cover search there.

---

## Development

```bash
make check        # fmt + vet + staticcheck + test — run this before finishing work
make fmt          # go fmt ./...
make vet          # go vet ./...
make staticcheck  # requires: go install honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck@latest
make lint         # requires golangci-lint
make test         # go test -race -count=1 -v ./...
```

Targeted runs:

```bash
go test ./internal/scraper/... -v                            # one package
go test ./internal/scraper/... -run TestShouldUseDynamic      # one test
go test ./test/... -v                                        # integration (mocks only)
go test ./internal/... ./pkg/... -coverprofile=coverage.out && go tool cover -func=coverage.out
```

Tests need no Redis and no Brave key — externals are mocked. Chromedp tests need a local Chromium. Package tests that exercise real log callbacks need `TestMain` calling `logger.Init("error")`.

**Swagger:** update handlers/structs, then run `swag init` (debug mode also regenerates on startup).

**Benchmarks:** `scripts/search-bench.py` (the numbers in the [search comparison](../../docs/SEARCH_COMPARISON.md)) and `scripts/load-harness.go`.

Conventions (error wrapping, context propagation, table-driven tests, `gofakeit` user agents) are written down in [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md). The full annotated tree lives in [Project structure](#project-structure).

---

## Docker image

Multi-stage build ([`Dockerfile`](Dockerfile)):

1. `golang:1.25-alpine` compiles `tomoshibi-api` and `tomoshibi-worker` (static, `CGO_ENABLED=0`)
2. `alpine:3.20` adds Chromium + fonts + `tini` (reaps Chrome's zombies) and sets `CHROME_BIN`/`CHROME_PATH`

```bash
docker build -t tomoshibi-api .
docker run --rm -p 7431:7431 \
  -e SERVER_MODE=release \
  -e REDIS_URL=redis://host.docker.internal:7434 \
  tomoshibi-api
```

Full stack from the repo root (`docker compose up -d`) also brings up Redis and SearXNG.

## Deploy

**Fly.io** — [`fly.toml`](fly.toml) (512 MB shared VM, `internal_port` 8080, `kill_timeout` 25s, health check on `/health`):

```bash
fly deploy
fly secrets set REDIS_URL=rediss://... BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY=... APP_API_KEYS=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
```

Keep `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` (default 20s) below `kill_timeout` so in-flight requests drain before the VM dies.

**Render** — [`render.yaml`](render.yaml).

---

## Local telemetry

Every search records one event (who answered, fallbacks, latency, trace id) and
every native engine attempt one more (ok/empty/blocked/timeout + reason) into
**daily JSONL files that never leave the machine**:

```text
data/telemetry/search-2026-11-14.jsonl   # one line per search
data/telemetry/engine-2026-11-14.jsonl   # one line per engine attempt
```

```bash
# scorecard: per-engine attempts, ok/empty/blocked, last_error, latency
curl -s 'localhost:7431/v1/insights?hours=24' | jq '.insights.engines'

# raw
cat data/telemetry/engine-*.jsonl | jq -s 'group_by(.engine) | map({engine: .[0].engine, n: length})'
```

Config (defaults): `TELEMETRY_ENABLED` (`true`) · `TELEMETRY_DIR`
(`data/telemetry`) · `TELEMETRY_RETAIN_DAYS` (`14`, `0` = keep forever). Docker
bind-mounts `./data:/app/data`, so the files survive container recreation.
`TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` makes `/v1/insights` answer `{"enabled": false}`
immediately.

This is the first thing to read when an engine starts misbehaving — the roster
rule is **no edit without a live probe**, and the scorecard is why: it is how
"the engine is broken" was distinguished from "the engine is blocked from this
address" (DuckDuckGo answered 30 times and refused 40 in one week, which is what
led to the browser search rung).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                               | Fix                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dynamic` mode fails / startup warning about Chromium | install a browser: `./install_browser.sh`, or `apt install chromium` / `brew install --cask chromium`. `CHROME_BIN` / `CHROME_PATH` override auto-detection. |
| `/v1/crawl` → `503`                                   | Redis isn't reachable — start it (`docker compose up -d redis`) or set `REDIS_URL`                                                                           |
| `/v1/batch/*`, `/v1/monitor` → `404`                  | same as above: those routes register only when Redis is configured                                                                                           |
| Swagger UI missing                                    | only served in `SERVER_MODE=debug`                                                                                                                           |
| `static` returns empty content on a React/Vue page    | expected — use `smart` (default) or `dynamic`; the SPA-shell heuristic triggers the Chromedp fallback                                                        |
| Outbound fetch refused as private/loopback            | SSRF guard — set `SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true` only for internal targets                                                                                         |
| Port already in use                                   | `SERVER_PORT=7432 go run ./cmd/api`                                                                                                                          |
| An engine stopped returning results                   | Read the scorecard first: `curl -s 'localhost:7431/v1/insights?hours=24' \| jq '.insights.engines'` → `blocked` / `last_error`. Confirm with a live probe (`CANARY_ENGINES=ddg go test -tags=canary ./internal/search/engines/ -run TestCanary -v`), log the verdict, then fix `internal/search/engines/registry.default.yaml` (`block_markers`, `proxy: webshare`, or `enabled: false`). **No roster edit without a live probe.** |
| A new error string shows up                            | Start from `recent_errors[].trace_id` in `/v1/insights` and grep that id in `docker logs`. The chain narrates itself: `backend failed, trying next`, `results concentrated on one domain` (weak-result gate), `proxy budget exhausted — engines degraded to direct egress`. |
| Search results look thin or off-topic                  | Check `backends` (who answered), `weak_gates` (native single-domain sets merged with fallbacks) and `engines.<name>.empty` (corpus mismatch). |
| `428` with `code: "consent-required"`                  | `transport: bridge` reached an origin the allowlist does not name: `tomoshibi bridge allow <host>`. |
| `502` with `code: "blocked"`                           | The site served a challenge (or the engine did). A human clears it in the bridge tab, then retry. Never returned as content. |
| My env var is ignored                                  | The api container takes an explicit `environment:` list (no `env_file`), and compose interpolation reads only the repo-root `.env` (gitignored). Add it in **both** places, then `docker compose up -d` — `--build` only when code changed. |
| `401` on `/v1/*`                                       | `APP_API_KEYS`/`API_KEYS` is set. Docker passes neither, so auth is off there. If you enable it, set `TOMOSHI_API_KEY` in your MCP config too. |
| Which search API keys do I need?                       | None — most engines are keyless. Optional boosts: `SERPER_API_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY`, `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`. Configure them in the **MCP** config and the backend receives them per request via `X-Tomoshi-Env` (`TOMOSHI_FORWARD_ENV=false` opts out). |
| MCP tools fail with `{}` or a raw `Invalid arguments` dump | `tomoshi` < 1.1.6 published a root-level `oneOf` schema clients rendered as empty properties. Upgrade and restart the MCP. |

## Why tomoshi?

If you're paying Firecrawl/Exa per token or spawning a browser per request, you're overpaying.

| What hurts with hosted APIs             | What tomoshi gives you                              | Outcome                             |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| **$0.01–0.10 per scrape** + rate limits | **$0 self-hosted** — one binary, hobby-tier RAM     | Ship RAG without a cloud bill       |
| **500ms Chrome spawn per request**      | **One shared allocator + recycled tabs**            | ~200ms static, parallel pools       |
| **JS SPAs return empty HTML**           | **Smart mode** — static first, fallback to Chromedp | Works on React/Vue without guessing |
| **Noisy HTML (nav/ads/footer)**         | **Readability main-content** + ad block             | Clean markdown your LLM wants       |

Part of [**Tomoshibi 灯火**](https://github.com/Michael-Obele/tomoshibi) — Go API + Svelte 5 playground + this MCP. Formerly Cinder.

---

## Install (30 seconds)

**Prerequisites:** A running Tomoshibi API. Host it in one command:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Michael-Obele/tomoshibi.git && cd tomoshibi
docker compose up -d  # api 7431 + redis 7434 (searxng: --profile searxng)
# or: fly deploy (see tomoshibi README)
```

Then add the MCP:

```jsonc
// .vscode/mcp.json or Claude config
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tomoshi": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "tomoshi"],
      "env": {
        "TOMOSHI_API_URL": "http://localhost:7431",
        // optional: forwarded to the backend as a search API key on every
        // request (X-Tomoshi-Env): set keys here, not in the backend's .env
        "BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY": "BSB-...",
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Legacy `CINDER_API_URL` still works. Aliases: `tomoshibi`, `tomoshibi-mcp` (same package).

Restart your editor — `tomoshi` appears as 3 tools.

---

## Run locally (development)

**Prerequisites:** [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.2+ and a running Tomoshibi API (`http://localhost:7431`).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Michael-Obele/tomoshibi.git && cd tomoshibi/packages/mcp
bun install
cp .env.example .env        # TOMOSHI_API_URL=http://localhost:7431

bun run dev                 # HTTP + SSE server → http://localhost:7433 (reloads on change)
bun run start               # same, without --watch
```

Two transports — pick one:

| Transport      | Command                                  | Use for                                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| **stdio**      | `npx -y tomoshi` (bin → `dist/stdio.js`) | local editors: VS Code, Claude, Cursor |
| **HTTP + SSE** | `bun run dev` on `PORT` (7433)           | remote / hosted clients                |

HTTP endpoints: `POST` `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP), `/sse` + `/message` (legacy SSE), `/health` and `GET /` (JSON status).

Checks and build:

```bash
bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
bun test            # unit tests
bun run check       # typecheck alias
bun run build       # dist/ — what the published bin runs
```

**Config** (see [.env.example](.env.example)): `TOMOSHI_API_URL` (required), `TOMOSHI_API_KEY`, `PORT`, `REDIS_URL` + `MCP_SESSION_MANAGER=redis` (sessions default to memory), `RATE_LIMIT_*`, `OAUTH_*`, `LOG_LEVEL`. Legacy `CINDER_API_URL` / `CINDER_API_KEY` still work.

**Search key forwarding:** names the backend asks for (`GET /v1/env`, e.g. `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`) are forwarded from this server's env on every request as `X-Tomoshi-Env`, so search API keys are configured once, here. `TOMOSHI_FORWARD_ENV` tunes it: `""` = all requested names (default), `"false"` = off, or a comma list to restrict. The backend re-validates against its own allowlist and resolves the keys per request; it never stores them.

---

## Docker

```bash
# from the repo root — starts on http://localhost:7433 (needs an API on 7431)
docker compose -f packages/mcp/docker-compose.yml up -d

curl http://localhost:7433/health
# → {"service":"tomoshi-mcp","status":"ok",...}
```

Point it somewhere else with `TOMOSHI_API_URL` (the name the server actually reads):

```bash
TOMOSHI_API_URL=https://your-api.example.com \
  docker compose -f packages/mcp/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

Published image:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 7433:7433 -e TOMOSHI_API_URL=http://host.docker.internal:7431 michaelobele/tomoshibi-mcp
```

## Tools

3 tools, not 8 — resource-oriented (`action` enum, ≤7 philosophy).

| Tool               | `action`                                                             | What it does                                                       |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `tomoshi_extract`  | `scrape` · `scrape_multi` (≤10) · `links` · `batch` · `batch_status` · `research` | Single/multi-page → markdown, link extraction, async batch (Redis), and a query → SERP → read pages |
| `tomoshi_discover` | `search` · `map` · `crawl` · `crawl_status`                          | Web search (native roster → SearXNG → **your browser** → Brave/Serper/Tavily), sitemap, async BFS crawl. `engine` picks a backend: `browser:ddg`, `browser:google`, `browser:bing` |
| `tomoshi_monitor`  | `create` · `status` · `delete`                                       | Hash markdown, webhook on change                                   |

Async actions (`batch`, `crawl`, `monitor`) are Redis-backed — poll `*_status` until done.

**Example — scrape + search in one turn:**

> `tomoshi_discover` `search` "svelte 5 runes" → `tomoshi_extract` `scrape_multi` on top 3 URLs → LLM-ready markdown

### Borrowing your own browser

`scrape` takes `transport`: `anonymous` (default) · `bridge` · `auto`. `bridge`
drives the browser you are signed into and needs **no recipe** — just a paired
[bridge extension](../bridge) and an allowed origin (`tomoshibi bridge allow
<host>`; the first touch answers `428 consent-required`). `auto` tries the cheap
lanes first and escalates into the browser only for an allowed origin.

Four named built-ins run in the page before it is read. A bare `true` is shorthand
for the defaults:

| Param | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `settle` | wait until the page stops moving (quiet DOM, stable height, no *finite* animation). Infinite spinners are excluded, or nothing ever settles |
| `scroll_collect` | scroll in steps and report what each round added — infinite feeds and lazy lists |
| `page_tree` | `dom` (works on Firefox) · `ax` (real accessibility tree) · `both` |
| `motion` | what animates, what is pinned, which element owns scrolling |

### Scrape params for JS-rendered extraction (dynamic mode)

| Param                   | Type               | Default | What it does                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | ------------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auto_extract`          | boolean            | `true`  | Harvest embedded page payloads (Next.js flight/`__NEXT_DATA__`, Nuxt, JSON-LD) into `extracted_data`; set `false` to disable. |
| `actions[].type`        | string             | -       | `wait_ms` · `wait_selector` · `click` · `scroll_down` · `scroll_to_bottom` · `wait_for_function` · `evaluate`.              |
| `actions[].script`      | string             | -       | JS for `evaluate` (expression; return value captured) or `wait_for_function` (predicate returning truthy).                 |
| `screenshot_opts.scale` | `"css" \| "device"` | `css`   | `css` = 1× device pixels (default, historical output); `device` = 2× device pixels (larger, crisper).                      |

Dynamic-mode responses also carry (omitted when empty):

- `evaluations` — `[{type, result, error, truncated}]`, one entry per `evaluate` action (plus a `{type: "wait_for_function", error}` entry when a wait fails; the remaining actions still run); a JS throw is recorded in `error` and the scrape continues (results > 256 KB are clipped).
- `extracted_data` — `{sources, canvases, truncated}`; each source is `{source, data}` (`__next_data`, `next_flight`, `__nuxt__`, `__initial_state__`, `json_ld`), capped at 512 KB total (8 sources × 128 KB).

Caps: actions ≤ 50/request; evaluate results ≤ 256 KB; extracted_data ≤ 512 KB (8 sources × 128 KB).

---

## Hosting

| Option             | Command                                                     | Cost              |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| **Docker Compose** | `docker compose -f packages/mcp/docker-compose.yml up -d`   | $0 (your machine) |
| **From source**    | `bun run dev` (MCP) + `go run ./packages/api/cmd/api` (API) | $0 + Chromium     |

API base: `http://localhost:7431` — all endpoints under `/v1` (`/scrape`, `/search`, `/crawl`, `/batch`, `/monitor`, `/map`).

## Project structure

```text
packages/mcp/
├── src/
│   ├── stdio.ts            # stdio entry — what `npx tomoshi` runs (via dist/stdio.js)
│   ├── index.ts            # HTTP + SSE entry (srvx) — /mcp · /sse · /health on PORT
│   ├── server.ts           # McpServer wiring — registers the 3 tools
│   ├── client.ts           # typed HTTP client over the Go API (shared by the tools)
│   ├── config.ts           # Valibot env schema — TOMOSHI_API_URL, PORT, OAuth, limits
│   ├── adapter.ts          # valibot → JSON Schema adapter for tool inputs
│   ├── auth-provider.ts    # optional OAuth 2.1 (SimpleProvider)
│   └── tools/              # one file per tool, colocated bun tests
│       ├── extract.ts      # tomoshi_extract  — scrape · scrape_multi · links · batch · batch_status
│       ├── discover.ts     # tomoshi_discover — search · map · crawl · crawl_status
│       ├── monitor.ts      # tomoshi_monitor  — create · status · delete
│       ├── schema.ts       # shared field builders (num, url, …)
│       └── *.test.ts       # bun test suites
├── dist/                   # build output — published to npm, backs the bins
├── Dockerfile              # deps stage → oven/bun:1-slim (non-root, wget healthcheck)
├── docker-compose.yml      # mcp on 7433, needs an API on 7431
├── package.json            # bin: tomoshi / tomoshibi / tomoshibi-mcp → dist/stdio.js
├── tsconfig.json           # typecheck config (bun run check)
├── tsconfig.build.json     # build config → dist/
└── .env.example            # TOMOSHI_API_URL, PORT, sessions, rate limits, OAuth
```

## Name

**tomoshi** (灯 — ともし) — Japanese for _lamp, light_. Short form of **Tomoshibi** (灯火 — ともしび) _lamp light_, the glow of a paper lantern. Search as illumination: lighting up the web for AI agents.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/Michael-Obele/tomoshibi/blob/main/LICENSE).

# Tomoshibi Web _(packages/web)_

Svelte 5 playground for Tomoshibi — a browser UI for scrape, crawl and search.

The browser playground for [**Tomoshibi 灯火**](../../README.md) — a SvelteKit UI that drives the scraping API: try a scrape, run a crawl, fire a search, read the docs, all from a local page.

- **Routes** — `/` homepage · `/playground` scrape/crawl/search UI · `/docs` API docs · `/login` password gate
- **Server-side proxy** — remote functions call the Go API from the server, so API keys never reach the browser
- **Rate limited** — global + per-IP + burst protection on every unauthenticated request
- **UI** — Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn-svelte-style components (Bits UI), lucide icons, dark/light mode

> Requires a running Tomoshibi API. See [`packages/api/README.md`](../api/README.md).

**Contents:** [Run locally](#run-locally) · [Run with Docker](#run-with-docker) · [Project structure](#project-structure) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) · [Related](#related)

---

## Run locally

**Prerequisites:** [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.2+ and the API on `http://localhost:7431`.

```bash
cd packages/web
bun install
cp .env.example .env          # required — see Config below
bun run dev                   # → http://localhost:5173
```

Start the API first (from `packages/api`: `go run ./cmd/api` or `docker compose up -d`).

### Config

`.env` in this directory (SvelteKit loads it automatically):

| Variable                      | Required | When read                                   | Purpose                                                            |
| ----------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `PRIVATE_TOMOSHI_BACKEND_URL` | **yes**  | **build/dev start** (`$env/static/private`) | API base URL, e.g. `http://localhost:7431`                         |
| `PRIVATE_TOMOSHI_API_KEY`     | no       | runtime                                     | API key, only if the API has `APP_API_KEYS` set                    |
| `MASTRA_PASSWORD`             | no       | runtime                                     | password for `/login`; the resulting cookie also skips rate limits |

> `PRIVATE_TOMOSHI_BACKEND_URL` is baked in when Vite starts — **restart `bun run dev` after changing it**, or the app throws `PRIVATE_TOMOSHI_BACKEND_URL is not set`. The other two are read per request.

### Scripts

| Command                           | What it does                               |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `bun run dev`                     | dev server on `5173`                       |
| `bun run build`                   | production build                           |
| `bun run preview`                 | serve the production build                 |
| `bun run check`                   | `svelte-kit sync` + `svelte-check` (types) |
| `bun run lint` / `bun run format` | Prettier check / write                     |

---

## Run with Docker

```bash
# from the repo root — serves on http://localhost:7432
docker compose -f packages/web/docker-compose.yml up -d

# point it at an API that isn't on this machine's localhost
PRIVATE_TOMOSHI_BACKEND_URL=http://192.168.1.10:7431 \
  docker compose -f packages/web/docker-compose.yml up -d --build
```

Details worth knowing:

- The backend URL is a **build argument** (`$env/static/private`), so the container URL is fixed at image build time — re-run `--build` when it changes. The compose file defaults to `http://host.docker.internal:7431` and maps `host.docker.internal` to the host gateway, so it reaches an API running outside Docker (e.g. the root `docker compose up -d` stack, or `go run ./cmd/api`).
- `MASTRA_PASSWORD` is a **runtime** env var — pass it with `-e MASTRA_PASSWORD=...` or add it to a `.env` next to the compose file.
- Image is two-stage: `oven/bun:1` builds (`DOCKER_BUILD=1` → `adapter-node`), `oven/bun:1-slim` serves `build/index.js` on port `7432`.

### With the rest of the stack

```bash
# 1. API + Redis + SearXNG
docker compose -f packages/api/docker-compose.yml up -d
# 2. this UI
docker compose -f packages/web/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

---

## Project structure

```text
packages/web/
├── src/
│   ├── routes/                 # SvelteKit file-based routing
│   │   ├── +page.svelte        # / — homepage: pitch, features, curl examples
│   │   ├── playground/         # /playground — interactive scrape / crawl / search UI
│   │   ├── docs/               # /docs — API documentation pages
│   │   ├── login/              # /login — password gate (MASTRA_PASSWORD)
│   │   ├── +layout.svelte      # app shell: nav, theme, toasts
│   │   └── layout.css          # Tailwind v4 theme tokens
│   ├── lib/
│   │   ├── remote/             # SvelteKit remote functions → server-side API proxy
│   │   ├── server/             # rate-limiter (global / IP / burst) + server helpers
│   │   ├── components/         # shadcn-svelte-style UI — ui/ · blocks/ · brand/
│   │   ├── hooks/              # reusable runes (is-mobile.svelte.ts)
│   │   ├── assets/             # images used by components
│   │   ├── docs-content.ts     # copy for the /docs pages
│   │   ├── index.ts            # barrel exports
│   │   └── utils.ts            # cn() — clsx + tailwind-merge
│   ├── hooks.server.ts         # auth cookie check + 3-tier rate limiting
│   ├── app.html / app.d.ts     # HTML shell + global types
├── static/                     # favicon.svg, robots.txt (served at /)
├── svelte.config.js            # adapter-auto (local) / adapter-node (DOCKER_BUILD=1)
├── vite.config.ts              # Vite + Tailwind + SvelteKit plugins
├── Dockerfile                  # bun build → bun:1-slim runtime, port 7432
├── docker-compose.yml          # web on 7432; backend URL passed as a build arg
├── package.json                # dev · build · preview · check · lint · format
└── .env.example                # PRIVATE_TOMOSHI_* + MASTRA_PASSWORD
```

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                  | Fix                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PRIVATE_TOMOSHI_BACKEND_URL is not set` | `cp .env.example .env` and set it, then restart the dev server                                                                               |
| Requests fail with connection refused    | the API isn't running — start it on `7431`, or point the URL at where it is                                                                  |
| `401` from the API                       | API auth is on — set `PRIVATE_TOMOSHI_API_KEY` in `.env`                                                                                     |
| Login always says incorrect credentials  | set `MASTRA_PASSWORD` in `.env`; it is compared strictly, with no default                                                                    |
| `429` / `503` while browsing             | rate limits hit (unauthenticated traffic is limited) — log in with `MASTRA_PASSWORD` or raise the limits in `src/lib/server/rate-limiter.ts` |
| Docker UI can't reach the API            | the URL is a build arg — `--build` after changing it; for a host API make sure `extra_hosts: host-gateway` is present (compose default)      |
| Port 5173 busy                           | `bun run dev -- --port 5174`                                                                                                                 |

## Bridge extension

# Tomoshibi Bridge

A small browser extension that lets your local [Tomoshibi](https://github.com/Michael-Obele/tomoshibi)
read and drive pages in the browser you are already signed into.

Tomoshibi cannot reach sites that know you: no cookies, a datacenter IP, a Go
TLS stack pretending to be Chrome. Modern bot protection scores whether all
those layers *agree*. The honest fix is not a sneakier bot; it is to be your
browser. That is all this extension does.

**New here?** [**docs/USAGE.md**](docs/USAGE.md) is the full walkthrough —
install, pair, the popup, every request field, every error code, and a
troubleshooting table. This README is the short version.

## What It Does

The extension opens one loopback WebSocket to Tomoshibi on `127.0.0.1` and
answers `fetch` messages by driving a real tab and reading it back:

- **Scripting** (default) — click, type, keys, scroll, navigate through the
  extension scripting API. No debugger, no infobar, no CDP tells; works on
  Firefox too.
- **turbo** (per-recipe `io: turbo`) — attaches `chrome.debugger` for trusted
  CDP input and full-page screenshots. Chrome only; shows the debugging infobar
  while a fetch runs.

A challenge page (Cloudflare, Turnstile, a login wall) stops the run as
*awaiting-human*: the tab stays open, you clear it, and the next fetch
proceeds. The bridge never solves a challenge and never types credentials.

## What it will not do

- No cookie access: `cookies`, `webRequest` and `nativeMessaging` are not in
  either manifest, and `bun test/e2e-protocol.ts` asserts they stay out.
- No credential typing, ever.
- No proxy rotation, no account pools, no solver.
- No reading tabs it was not asked about; one pinned tab per origin, opened on
  demand.
- No answering a server it has not verified: the extension releases its token
  only after the process on the port proves it holds the key from pairing.

## Install

1. Start Tomoshibi (the bridge is built in):
   `go run ./cmd/api` from `packages/api`, or the Docker image.
2. Build this directory: `bun install && bun run build`. It compiles to
   `.output/chrome-mv3` (Firefox: `bun run build:firefox` →
   `.output/firefox-mv3`).
3. Load the build as an unpacked extension: `chrome://extensions` → Developer
   mode → **Load unpacked** → pick `.output/chrome-mv3` (not this directory — it
   holds the sources, not the extension).
4. Run `tomoshibi bridge code` (or read the startup log) and type the 6-digit
   code into the extension popup. One pairing per browser; the token is stored
   locally and revoked with `tomoshibi bridge unpair` (or by deleting
   `~/.config/tomoshi/bridge.json`, which the running server notices).

You are now ready. **A recipe is not required.**

**Firefox:** build with `bun run build:firefox` and load
`.output/firefox-mv3` through `about:debugging` → This Firefox → Load Temporary
Add-on. The Firefox build has no `debugger` permission, so `io: turbo` recipes
fail with a readable message while the scripting layer keeps working.

## Recipe-free use (the normal path)

Ask for the browser on the request itself:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7431/v1/scrape \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/dashboard","transport":"bridge"}'
```

- `transport: "bridge"` drives the browser. `"auto"` tries the anonymous lanes
  first and escalates into the browser only when the answer is a block or a shell.
- An origin the server does not know yet answers **428 `consent-required`** with
  the origin. That is the gate, not a bug:

  ```bash
  tomoshibi bridge allow example.com      # or *.example.com
  tomoshibi bridge allowed                # what is allowed now
  tomoshibi bridge deny example.com
  ```

  A fresh install already allows the three search hosts (DuckDuckGo, Google,
  Bing) and nothing else — deliberately not `*.google.com`, which would include
  mail.
- `tomoshibi bridge status` shows the pairing and the allowlist.
- A page budget (600 pages/hour, `BRIDGE_PAGES_PER_HOUR`) caps a runaway loop.

Recipes are the specialization, not the price of admission: use one when a site
needs its own actions, its own extraction schema, its own pace, or `io: turbo`.

## Search without a search API

The same browser rung turns the engines that block a datacenter address back on.
The engine telemetry in `data/telemetry` is the reason this exists: DuckDuckGo
returns `blocked` more often than `ok` from this machine's own egress.

```bash
# switch engines per request
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7431/v1/search \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"svelte 5 runes","engine":"browser:ddg"}'

# or ask for pages, not just links
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7431/v1/research \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"svelte 5 runes","engine":"browser:google","pages":5,"summary":true}'
```

`browser:ddg`, `browser:google` and `browser:bing` are accepted; omit `engine`
for the configured chain, which puts the free engines first and the paid API
last. `research` returns the SERP and the read pages together, with
`paid_api_used` telling you what it actually cost.

The popup also holds the API port (default `7431`), the pairing code box, and a
pause switch. The toolbar badge says which state it is in: green `on` means
paired and connected, amber `pair` means connected but unpaired, grey-red `off`
means no connection, red `err` means the last attempt failed (the popup shows
why).

The manifest asks for `host_permissions: ["<all_urls>"]`, because a recipe may
name any host. Nothing is read until a fetch names a URL.

## Security notes

- The socket is loopback-only, and Tomoshibi refuses any `http(s)` origin: a
  web page in your own browser is a loopback peer too, so only extension
  origins (and clients that send no Origin at all) are accepted.
- Pairing is mutual. The code rotates every 10 minutes, works once, and ten
  wrong guesses burn it; the extension verifies the server's proof with the
  code you typed before it stores anything.
- Every fetch is written to Tomoshibi's `access.log.jsonl`: recipe, lane,
  origin, result.
- Fetches refuse to drive a page that has left the origin they asked for, and a
  scripting-layer screenshot is skipped if another tab becomes active first.
- `debugger` permission exists for the turbo layer only. If you never use
  `io: turbo` recipes, delete it from `wxt.config.ts` and drop `runTurbo` from
  `entrypoints/background/index.ts`.

## Development

WXT builds it. `bun run dev` starts Chrome with the extension loaded and HMR;
`bun run check` is the typecheck plus the unit tests.

To get something you can actually install:

```bash
bun run zip            # .output/tomoshibibridge-<version>-chrome.zip and -firefox.zip
bun run verify:build   # asserts MV3 both targets, version matches package.json,
                       # no forbidden permission, both zips present
```

CI runs both on every change to this package and uploads the zips as a build
artifact; a `bridge-v*` tag attaches them to a GitHub release. There is no icon
yet, so the toolbar shows the default puzzle piece.

`AGENTS.md` is the contract for anyone changing this repo: the commands, the
rules that tests enforce, and what a change here forces on the Tomoshibi side.
`docs/product.md` is the plan for turning this spike into the product.

```bash
bun test/e2e-protocol.ts     # protocol against the real API, ~40s, no browser
tomoshibi recipes verify     # replay recipe fixtures offline
```

The protocol test builds the Go binaries itself and plays a scripted extension
over the real WebSocket. The full-stack test launches this extension in a real
browser, pairs it through the popup, and drives it through a fixture site
(`fixtures/` holds the two pages the scripted extension serves):

```bash
bun test/e2e-extension.ts    # ~60s; see the note below about which Chrome
```

That test needs a Chromium that honours `--load-extension`. Branded Google
Chrome 137+ ignores it (and its CDP replacement, `Extensions.loadUnpacked`,
registers the extension without ever starting its service worker — every
`chrome-extension://` page answers `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`). Install Chrome for
Testing or Chromium and point `CHROME_BIN` at it, or let the test find the copy
Playwright already keeps in `~/.cache/ms-playwright`. It also needs a Go
toolchain, and it uses ports 7439, 7445 and 9444 plus `/tmp/tomoshibi-e2e`.

## What it is, and when you want it

Tomoshibi fetches as a stranger: no cookies, a datacenter address, a Go TLS stack
wearing a Chrome handshake. Sites that know you refuse it — and the ones that
don't still hand back a login wall.

The bridge fixes that by not being a scraper at all. It is a browser extension
that opens one loopback socket to your local Tomoshibi and, when asked, opens a
real tab in the browser **you are already signed into**, reads it, and hands the
result back.

Reach for it when:

- the page is behind a login you already have,
- the site blocks datacenter or headless traffic,
- the page only works with your session (a dashboard, a subscription, a forum),
- a search engine refuses Tomoshibi's address — which is most of them
  (see [Search](#search-and-research-through-your-browser)).

Do **not** reach for it for ordinary public pages. `static`/`dynamic` is faster,
lighter, and doesn't open a window on your screen.

## Install

You need Tomoshibi running locally, and an extension build.

### 1. Tomoshibi

```bash
docker compose up -d                       # from the repo root
# or
go run ./packages/api/cmd/api             # needs Go 1.25+ and Chromium
```

The bridge is built into the API — nothing extra to enable. It starts a
loopback listener and prints a pairing code at startup.

### 2. The extension

**Chrome or Edge** — download `tomoshibibridge-<version>-chrome.zip` from the
[latest `bridge-v*` release](https://github.com/Michael-Obele/tomoshibi/releases),
unzip it, then:

1. open `chrome://extensions`
2. turn on **Developer mode** (top right)
3. **Load unpacked** → pick the unzipped directory

Chrome cannot install a `.zip` directly; the unzip step is not optional.

**Firefox** — download `tomoshibibridge-<version>-firefox.zip`, then
`about:debugging` → **This Firefox** → **Load Temporary Add-on** → pick the zip.
Firefox drops temporary add-ons when it restarts, so this is a per-session
install by design.

**From source** — in `packages/bridge`:

```bash
bun install && bun run zip      # .output/*-chrome.zip and *-firefox.zip
bun run verify:build            # assert the build is the one we meant to ship
```

`bun run build` / `bun run build:firefox` produce unpacked directories
(`.output/chrome-mv3`, `.output/firefox-mv3`) if you'd rather load those.

### What "loaded" looks like

The toolbar shows the Tomoshibi puzzle piece (there is no icon yet) with a badge.
A fresh install shows a grey/red **`off`** badge until Tomoshibi is running, then
amber **`pair`**.

## Pair

Pairing is one-time per browser, and it is mutual: the extension also verifies
that whatever is listening on the port really holds the key from pairing.

```bash
tomoshibi bridge code        # 6 digits, also printed in the API's startup log
```

Paste them into the popup's **6-digit code** box and press **Pair this browser**.

Facts worth knowing:

- The code **rotates every 10 minutes**, and again after every successful pair —
  a code works exactly once.
- **Ten wrong guesses burn it.** Ask for a new one.
- The server stores only a SHA-256 of each token; the plaintext token exists once,
  in the reply the extension saves. It goes out only after the server proves it
  holds the pairing key, so a process that squats on the port gets neither.
- `tomoshibi bridge status` lists paired browsers with last-seen times.
- `tomoshibi bridge unpair` revokes them (or `unpair <name>` for one). A running
  server re-reads the state file, so the revocation lands on a live socket.

**Re-pairing.** If you delete `~/.config/tomoshi/bridge.json`, reinstall
Tomoshibi, or move to a machine with fresh state, the old token stops working and
the popup shows `err` with an explanation. Delete the pairing in the popup
(**Forget**) and pair again. **Forget** also clears the extension's local token,
which is what you want before handing the browser to someone else.

## The popup, control by control

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Dot + sentence** | Connection state in one line: not connected / connected but unpaired / connected and paired |
| **6-digit code** + **Pair this browser** | Shown only while connected and unpaired |
| **Pause (stop answering fetches)** | Stops answering *fetches* without disconnecting. Takes effect on the next action of a run that is already going |
| **Allowed origins** | The server's allowlist, read-only, first four with a `+n` count |
| **Last run** | Origin, action count and duration of the most recent fetch |
| **Tomoshibi port** + **Save port** | The API port, default `7431`. Change it if you run Tomoshibi elsewhere |
| **Forget** | Drop the local token and reconnect. The way out of a bad pairing |
| **Red line at the bottom** | The last error, in words |

## The toolbar badge

| Badge | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| grey/red **`off`** | No connection to Tomoshibi | Is the API running? Is the port right? |
| amber **`pair`** | Connected, not paired | `tomoshibi bridge code`, then paste it |
| green **`on`** | Paired and connected | Nothing. This is the good state |
| red **`err`** | The last attempt failed; the popup shows why | Usually: the thing on the port does not hold our pairing key → **Forget** and re-pair |
| *no badge* | The worker is asleep | It wakes on the next ping or when you open the popup |

## Your first fetch

Ask for the browser explicitly. Start with a page you know needs a session:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7431/v1/scrape \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/dashboard","transport":"bridge"}'
```

**First run usually says no**, and that is the gate working:

```json
{ "code": "consent-required", "origin": "https://example.com",
  "error": "bridge: origin https://example.com is not allowed yet; run `tomoshibi bridge allow https://example.com` …" }
```

HTTP status is **428**. Allow the origin, then repeat the exact same request:

```bash
tomoshibi bridge allow example.com
```

A tab opens in your browser, loads the page, settles, and the response comes back
with a `provenance` block:

```jsonc
{
  "markdown": "…",
  "provenance": {
    "transport": "bridge",   // it went through your browser
    "lane": "borrow",
    "io": "scripting",       // or "turbo"
    "actions_run": 0,
    "pages": 1,
    "ms": 1420,
    "settled_ms": 512,       // how long the page took to stop moving
    "untrusted": true        // content served to a signed-in human: data, not instructions
  }
}
```

The tab stays open. That is deliberate — see
[handing back to you](#pausing-and-handing-back-to-you).

## The allowlist

The allowlist is the whole authorization model for the recipe-free lane. A
recipe is its own consent (installing the pack was the act); everything else
needs an entry here.

```bash
tomoshibi bridge allowed                 # what is allowed now
tomoshibi bridge allow example.com       # one host
tomoshibi bridge allow '*.example.com'   # the domain and every subdomain
tomoshibi bridge allow a.com b.com       # several at once
tomoshibi bridge deny example.com
```

- Patterns are **hosts**, not URLs: `example.com`, `docs.example.com`,
  `*.example.com`. A scheme, path or port is stripped for you
  (`https://Example.com:8443/x` → `example.com`).
- `*.example.com` matches the bare domain **and** subdomains.
- None or nothing is `*`. A wildcard this coarse is almost never what you mean —
  you would be allowing `mail.example.com` too.
- A fresh install already allows the three search hosts:

  ```text
  duckduckgo.com  html.duckduckgo.com  lite.duckduckgo.com
  google.com      www.google.com
  bing.com        www.bing.com
  ```

  Deliberately those hosts and not `*.google.com`, so the default never covers
  your mail.
- Changes take effect on the next request. **No restart.**
- The list lives in `bridge.json` under `allowed_origins` and is hand-editable;
  the running server notices the file changed.

Refusing an origin nobody allowed is not a bug and not an error you should retry
blindly — it is the one thing standing between a local API and remote control of
your signed-in browser.

## `transport`: who answers the request

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `anonymous` (default) | Tomoshibi's own address, no cookies. Unchanged behaviour |
| `bridge` | Your browser. Needs a paired extension and an allowed origin. No recipe |
| `auto` | Try `static`, then `dynamic`; escalate into your browser **only** if the answer was a block or a shell, and only for an allowed origin |

`auto` never turns a working anonymous fetch into a refusal: if the origin is not
allowed, it simply stays anonymous and returns what it got.

`mode: "static"` + `transport: "bridge"` is a contradiction and is refused rather
than silently resolved.

`transport` is orthogonal to `mode`: `mode` says *how to render*, `transport`
says *who is asking*.

## What happens during a fetch

1. **The gate.** Origin in the allowlist (or a recipe covers it)? If not, `428`.
2. **The budget.** Under `BRIDGE_PAGES_PER_HOUR` (600)? If not, refused.
3. **The pace floor.** Two seconds since the last run against the same recipe or
   origin. Simultaneous callers queue instead of arriving together.
4. **The tab.** One pinned tab per origin, created on first use and reused. It is
   visible on purpose — you are the override.
5. **Actions**, if you asked for any, in order. Failed actions are advisory: one
   dead click does not lose an otherwise readable page.
6. **`scroll_collect`**, if you asked for it.
7. **`settle`** — until the DOM is quiet, the scroll height is stable, and no
   finite animation is running.
8. **Read** `document.body.innerText` and `document.documentElement.outerHTML`
   (8 MB HTML / 2 MB text caps).
9. **Challenge markers.** If the page matches a known interstitial, the run stops
   as `awaiting-human` and the tab is left for you.
10. **`page_tree` / `motion`**, if you asked for them.
11. **Screenshot**, if you asked for it.
12. The server re-checks the origin and marks the result `untrusted`, never cached.

The built-in markers are: `Just a moment...`, `Enable JavaScript and cookies to
continue`, `Checking your browser before accessing`, `Verifying you are human`,
`Attention Required!`, `cf-challenge-running`. A recipe may add more via
`expect.absent`.

## Pausing, and handing back to you

Two different things, often confused:

**Pause** is yours. Flip the switch in the popup and the bridge stops answering
fetches immediately; a run already going stops before its next action and reports
`paused`. Nothing is lost — resume and retry.

**`awaiting-human`** is the site's. A challenge wall, a consent gate, a 2FA prompt
— the bridge does not solve it. It stops, marks the response `awaiting-human`
(`502`, `code: "blocked"`, `vendor: "bridge-handoff"`), and **leaves the tab open**.
You clear whatever it is, then retry the same request. The tab is already pinned
and already solved, so the retry usually succeeds first time.

The line: the bridge uses access you already have; it never defeats a control you
don't.

## The extraction built-ins

Four fixed functions that run in the page before it is read. A closed vocabulary
on purpose — no caller-supplied JavaScript reaches a signed-in tab.

| Field | What it does | Reach for it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `settle` | Waits until the page stops moving: DOM quiet, scroll height stable, no *finite* animation running. Reports `provenance.settled_ms` | Always useful. Infinite spinners are excluded, or nothing would ever settle |
| `scroll_collect` | Scrolls in steps and reports what each round added | Infinite feeds, lazy lists, "load more" pages |
| `page_tree` | The page outline: `dom` (tag, role, path, box, visibility — works on Firefox) or `ax` (the real accessibility tree — Chrome/turbo), or `both` | You need structure, not text: what is a nav, what is a list, what is actually visible |
| `motion` | What is animating (infinite flagged), what is fixed/sticky, which element owns scrolling | Before parsing a page of carousels and sticky headers |

`settle` is on by default on the generic path — a fixed sleep is a guess.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7431/v1/scrape -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "url": "https://example.com/feed",
  "transport": "bridge",
  "settle": { "quiet_ms": 400, "max_ms": 8000 },
  "scroll_collect": { "max_rounds": 8, "item_selector": "article" },
  "page_tree": "dom",
  "motion": true
}'
```

| Option | Defaults | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `settle.quiet_ms` / `max_ms` / `poll_ms` | 500 / 10000 / 120 | How long the DOM must be quiet, and the ceiling |
| `scroll_collect.max_rounds` / `quiet_rounds` | 8 / 3 | Stops after N rounds with no growth |
| `scroll_collect.step_px` / `pause_ms` | ~0.9 viewport / 350 | Distance per round, wait after each |
| `scroll_collect.item_selector` | — | The repeated element that defines "an item". The precise growth signal |
| `page_tree_options.max_nodes` / `max_depth` / `min_text_len` | 1200 / 12 / 0 | Caps on the outline |

Responses gain `page_tree`, `motion` and `collected`, and `provenance.settled_ms`.
All optional; ordinary pages come back exactly as before.

## Screenshots

```jsonc
{ "screenshot": true, "screenshot_opts": { "full_page": true } }
```

| Layer | Captures |
| --- | --- |
| `scripting` (default) | The **viewport only** — `tabs.captureVisibleTab` has no beyond-viewport mode. `screenshot_opts.full_page` is reported honestly as `false` |
| `turbo` (recipe with `io: turbo`) | Full page, `captureBeyondViewport` |

A scripting-layer screenshot is skipped (and says so in `provenance.actions_failed`)
if another tab becomes active first — the alternative is screenshotting someone
else's page.

## Recipes: when you actually need one

**Most uses need none.** A recipe is the specialization for a site the generic
driver cannot handle:

- it needs its own navigation steps (click this, type that, press Enter),
- it needs its own extraction schema,
- it needs its own pace,
- it needs `io: turbo` (trusted CDP input, full-page screenshots, `evaluate`,
  `wait_for_function`).

```bash
tomoshibi recipes add <dir|git-url>   # verify hashes, install
tomoshibi recipes list                # what is installed
tomoshibi recipes verify <pack>       # replay saved fixtures, no network
tomoshibi recipes remove <pack>
```

A pack that no longer parses fails `verify` before it ever drives a browser —
that is what stops silent garbage when a site redesigns.

Two rules worth remembering:

- **A recipe must cover the host it is applied to.** An explicit recipe id naming
  a foreign host is an error, not a shortcut.
- **A recipe is its own consent.** You do not also need an allowlist entry.

`io: turbo` requires Chrome: the Firefox build has no `debugger` permission and
says so instead of falling back silently.

Pack format, the `expect` contract and the full schema: see the
[API README's recipes section](../../api/README.md#recipes).

## Search and research through your browser

The same rung turns search engines that block a datacenter address back on. This
is the reason the bridge exists for many people: DuckDuckGo answered **30 times
and refused 40** from this machine's own address in one week.

```bash
# one engine, chosen per request
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7431/v1/search -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"svelte 5 runes","engine":"browser:ddg"}'

# the query AND the pages behind it
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7431/v1/research -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"svelte 5 runes","engine":"browser:google","pages":5,"summary":true}'
```

- `engine` accepts `browser:ddg`, `browser:google`, `browser:bing`. Omit it for
  the configured chain, which puts the free engines first and the paid API last.
- `research` returns `results`, `pages`, `failures`, `elapsed_ms` and
  `paid_api_used` — so you can see what a query actually cost.
- An engine challenge is `502` with `code: "awaiting-human"` on both endpoints.
  Never a 500, never an empty list pretending the query had no answers.
- Google serves a consent wall to a profile that has not answered it. The bridge
  clicks the explicit **Accept all** control once, and the cookie does the rest.

## From an agent

The MCP exposes all of this as tool parameters:

```jsonc
// tomoshi_extract
{
  "action": "scrape",
  "url": "https://example.com/dashboard",
  "transport": "bridge",     // or "auto"
  "settle": true,
  "page_tree": "dom",
  "motion": true
}

// tomoshi_extract — one query, then the pages
{ "action": "research", "query": "svelte 5 runes", "engine": "browser:ddg", "pages": 5 }

// tomoshi_discover — engine switching
{ "action": "search", "query": "…", "engine": "browser:bing" }
```

`settle` and `scroll_collect` accept `true` as shorthand for the defaults. Full
tool reference: [packages/mcp/README.md](../../mcp/README.md).

## Security and privacy

What the extension **cannot** do — enforced in the manifest and asserted by tests
in CI:

- **No cookie access.** `cookies`, `webRequest`, `nativeMessaging`,
  `externally_connectable`, `history` and `bookmarks` are not in either manifest.
- **No credential typing, ever.** Password, passcode, one-time-code, card fields,
  and anything named `pwd` / `pin` / `otp` / `2fa` / `cvv` are refused at the
  field level, in both layers.
- **No challenge solving**, no proxy rotation, no account pools.
- **No reading tabs it wasn't asked about.** One pinned tab per origin, opened on
  demand.
- **No remote code.** Everything it runs ships in the zip.

How the connection is protected:

- The socket is **loopback-only**, and Tomoshibi refuses any `http(s)` origin — a
  web page in your own browser is a loopback peer too.
- **Mutual auth.** The extension releases its token only to a process that proves
  it holds the key from pairing. A squatter on the port gets nothing.
- **Origin drift is refused.** If the page navigates somewhere other than the
  origin you asked for, the run stops rather than reading another site with your
  session.
- **Every fetch is logged** to `~/.config/tomoshi/access.log.jsonl` — recipe,
  lane, origin, result.

Your session never leaves the machine. Nothing is exported, synced or tunneled.

## Limits

| Limit | Value | Override |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pages per hour, borrow lane | 600 | `BRIDGE_PAGES_PER_HOUR` (`0` disables) |
| Actions per page | 64 | — |
| HTML read | 8 MB | — |
| Text read | 2 MB | — |
| One frame | 24 MiB | protocol constant |
| Pace floor between runs | 2 s per recipe/origin | recipe `access.pace.min_interval_ms` |
| Per-page timeout | 60 s | recipe `request.timeout_ms` |

The budget exists because a research loop with a bug should cost a refusal, not a
hundred tabs on a real session.

## Troubleshooting

### By what you see

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Badge `off` | No connection | Is the API running? Is the port in the popup right? Is another Tomoshibi holding the port? |
| Badge `pair`, no pair box | Not connected yet | The pair box appears only once the socket is up |
| Badge `err`, "it does not hold our pairing key" | The server was reinstalled or its state deleted | Popup → **Forget** → `tomoshibi bridge code` → pair again |
| The code is rejected | Codes rotate every 10 min, work once, and burn after 10 wrong guesses | Get a fresh one |
| A tab opens and the fetch fails | Expected on the first crack at a new origin | Check the error code below |
| Nothing happens at all | The worker is asleep, or the extension was reloaded | Open the popup (wakes it), or toggle the extension off/on |
| Chrome refuses to load the folder | You picked the source directory | Pick `.output/chrome-mv3` (or the unzipped release folder), not the package folder |

### By error code

| Code | HTTP | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `consent-required` | 428 | Origin is not in the allowlist | `tomoshibi bridge allow <host>` |
| `bridge-offline` | 502 | No browser connected | Start Chrome with the extension loaded; check the badge |
| `bridge-unpaired` | 502 | Connected but not paired | Pair in the popup |
| `bridge-timeout` | 502 | The browser did not answer in time | The tab may be stuck loading — check it |
| `bridge-disconnected` | 502 | The socket dropped mid-fetch | Retry; usually a browser restart |
| `paused` | 502 | The pause switch is on | Flip it off in the popup |
| `blocked` (with `vendor`) | 502 | A challenge page was served | Clear it in the open tab, then retry |
| `blocked` + `vendor: bridge-handoff` | 502 | `awaiting-human`: a marker matched | Same — solve it in the tab, retry |
| `awaiting-human` | 502 | An engine served its own interstitial | Clear it in the bridge tab, retry the query |

`provenance.actions_failed` names every action the browser refused, with the
reason. A page that came back does not tell you that half a recipe was skipped;
that field does.

### Turning up the detail

```bash
tomoshibi bridge status        # port, paired devices, last seen
tomoshibi access log -n 20     # the last 20 fetches: recipe, lane, origin, result
```

## Files, environment and commands

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| State: pairing code, port, device token hashes, server key, allowlist | `~/.config/tomoshi/bridge.json` (mode `0600`) |
| Audit log: one line per fetch | `~/.config/tomoshi/access.log.jsonl` |
| The same dir, elsewhere | `BRIDGE_STATE_DIR` |

```
tomoshibi bridge code                 print the current pairing code and port
tomoshibi bridge status               paired devices and last-seen times
tomoshibi bridge unpair [name|all]    revoke a paired browser (default: all)
tomoshibi bridge allow  <host...>     add to the recipe-free allowlist
tomoshibi bridge deny   <host...>     remove from it
tomoshibi bridge allowed              print it
tomoshibi recipes add <dir|git-url>   verify and install a pack
tomoshibi recipes list                installed packs and their recipes
tomoshibi recipes verify [id]         offline fixture check (no network)
tomoshibi recipes remove <pack>       uninstall a pack (name@sha)
tomoshibi access log [-n N]           the last N access-log lines (default 20)
```

Environment variables that matter to this feature:

| Variable | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BRIDGE_STATE_DIR` | `~/.config/tomoshi` | Where state and the audit log live |
| `BRIDGE_PAGES_PER_HOUR` | `600` | Borrow-lane page budget; `0` disables |
| `SERVER_PORT` | `7431` | The bridge listener is mounted on the API server itself, at `/bridge` — there is no separate bridge port |

## Uninstall

1. `tomoshibi bridge unpair` — revoke every browser. Takes effect on live sockets.
2. Remove the extension: `chrome://extensions` → Remove, or `about:debugging` →
   Remove.
3. Optionally `rm ~/.config/tomoshi/bridge.json` and `access.log.jsonl`.

Pairing is one browser at a time; uninstalling from one Chrome does not affect
another.

## FAQ

**Do I need a recipe?** No. `transport: "bridge"` is enough once the origin is
allowed.

**Does it open a window every time?** Yes — one pinned tab per origin, reused
across fetches. Visible on purpose: you are the override.

**Can it run unattended?** Not for the borrow lane. Crawl and monitor deliberately
refuse it: a crawl follows links nobody chose (one could be a sign-out link) and a
monitor repeats unattended.

**Will it get my account banned?** It uses your real session at a human-ish pace
with a page budget. That is the least suspicious option available — but it is
still automation, and the site's terms are the site's terms.

**Why does Google ask me to accept cookies once?** A fresh profile hits Google's
consent wall. The bridge clicks the explicit **Accept all** control a person would
click, once; the cookie then persists in your profile.

**Does the browser have to stay open?** Yes. Whole point.

**Can I use it from another machine?** The socket is loopback-only and refuses
web origins. Remote use means a tunnel to Tomoshibi, not to the browser — and that
is not built.

**Firefox support?** Yes, scripting layer only. `io: turbo` needs Chrome's
`debugger` API.
